description: Harness Kit JSON-RPC wire contract. Generated from core Go types; run make generate. x-rpc-methods binds parameter and result schemas; x-event-payloads binds discriminators to payload schemas.

AcpRuntimeSettings.description:
ACPRuntime configures a named external ACP agent. Process wiring applies at
startup; model and native session selections use the session settings group.
Omitted limits use the adapter defaults. Set process.runtimes to select which
configured agents are registered. The process.acp map is replaced as a whole.

ApprovalKind.description: Kind classifies what an approval request is about.

ApprovalRequest.description: Request describes an action awaiting approval.

input.description: Input is the raw, runtime-specific tool input.

outcomes.description: Outcomes lists the outcomes the runtime can honour. Empty means all.

reason.description: Reason is the agent's explanation, when it gives one.

title.description: Title is a one-line, human-readable summary suitable for a prompt.

tool.description: Tool is the runtime's name for the tool, e.g. "Bash" or "commandExecution".

ApprovalResolvedData.description: ApprovalResolvedData is the payload of approval.resolved.

request.description:
Request is included when the request was decided without being
announced (Source == policy), so observers can audit it.

ApprovalSource.description: Source records who produced a decision.

AuthState.description: AuthState is the authentication state reported by a runtime.

AuthStatus.description:
AuthStatus describes how a runtime is signed in. It deliberately omits
personal data such as email addresses.

method.description:
Method is the runtime's own name for the auth method, e.g.
"chatgpt", "apiKey", "claude.ai", "api_key".

plan.description: Plan is the subscription plan, when the runtime reports it.

BudgetExceeded.description: BudgetExceededData identifies the observed threshold that stopped further work.

BudgetLimits.description: BudgetLimits are host policy. Nil disables a limit; zero admits no further work.

BudgetLimitsPatch.description: BudgetLimits are host policy. Nil disables a limit; zero admits no further work.

BudgetUsage.description:
BudgetUsage contains observed totals. Incomplete totals are lower bounds; nil cost
means no cost estimate was supplied. Reported costs are estimates, not bills.

approvals.description: Approvals: can pause and ask the host to approve actions.

cancel.description: Cancel: an in-progress turn can be interrupted gracefully.

compaction.description:
Compaction means the adapter can request native compaction. Per-session
availability is negotiated through Compactor.CanCompact.

configuration.description: Configuration advertises accepted settings and their lifetimes.

contextUsage.description: ContextUsage reports model-window observations separately from spend.

images.description: Images: image input parts are accepted by the runtime.

listSessions.description:
ListSessions: implements SessionLister (lists the runtime's own
stored sessions, including ones started outside Harness Kit).

resume.description: Resume: sessions can be resumed by runtime session ID.

streaming.description: Streaming: emits message.delta events while the agent writes.

usage.description: Usage: reports consumed token usage, not just context-window occupancy.

CompactionSettings.description:
CompactionSettings controls additional host-requested compaction before a
prompt. Nil thresholds leave timing to the native runtime. Neither setting
disables a runtime's own automatic compaction. Either threshold can trigger.

CompactionSettingsPatch.description:
CompactionSettings controls additional host-requested compaction before a
prompt. Nil thresholds leave timing to the native runtime. Neither setting
disables a runtime's own automatic compaction. Either threshold can trigger.

ConfigPatch.description:
Patch changes only supplied fields. Empty strings explicitly clear portable
selections; false, zero, null and empty lists remain native option values.
Reset names a field to inherit again: model, effort or options.NAME.
Session patches inherit creation settings; turn patches inherit current
session settings. A field cannot be both set and reset in the same patch.

ConfigurationSupport.description:
Support describes where a setting can be supplied. Session changes apply to
future turns, even when submitted during a turn. Live requires an explicit
active-turn API; a setting without Live never changes a running turn.

ContextCompactionData.description:
ContextCompactionData reports manual, threshold-triggered, and observed native
compaction using one lifecycle. Runtime-specific details remain in runtime.status.

ContextUsageData.description:
ContextUsageData is the latest model-window observation, independent of
cumulative token consumption. Nil counts are unknown; zero is a known zero.
Basis is reported (native occupancy), last_request (the latest model request)
or unknown. Stale observations must not be presented as current occupancy.

hostTools.description:
HostTools limits the session to these registered host tools (default
all); DisableHostTools gives it none, and no Harness Kit bridge.

mcp.description:
MCP adds MCP servers for this session (portable format; see the mcp
package). A sidecar started with --kit-mcp also merges the user and
trusted project config files.

settings.description: Settings uses the shared schema. Only the session section is accepted here.

title.description: Title names the session; empty means the start of the first prompt.

message.description: Message is passed back to the agent (e.g. why it was denied).

updatedInput.description:
UpdatedInput optionally replaces the tool input, for runtimes that
support editing a request before approving it.

Discovery.description: Discovery is the result of probing a runtime.

notes.description: Notes are non-blocking information, such as usage-policy reminders.

problems.description: Problems are blocking issues (not installed, unsupported version...).

ready.description:
Ready is true when the runtime is installed, not known to be signed
out, and has no blocking problems.

Empty.description: Empty is the result of methods that return nothing.

code.description: Code is a stable, machine-readable identifier (e.g. "runtime_exited").

EventPage.description:
EventPage is a bounded transcript page. NextSeq is the last returned event's
sequence, or the supplied cursor for an empty page. HasMore means another
stored event follows; Truncated reports unavailable history, not pagination.

ForkSessionOptions.description:
ForkParams branch the complete conversation. Arbitrary turn cutoffs are not
portable across runtimes. Settings use the same envelope as session creation.

GitDiffParams.description:
Git methods accept a session ID. The host resolves its saved repository; a
client cannot substitute an arbitrary filesystem root in a request.

GitFileStatus.description:
FileStatus uses Git's porcelain status letters. Paths are repository-relative
literal paths, not pathspec patterns. OriginalPath is present for renames.

GitRemoteOptions.description:
RemoteParams chooses a configured remote by name. Empty fields use Git's
configured upstream. Push never forces and Pull only fast-forwards.

GitSettings.description:
GitSettings is the git group of the shared settings document. Each operation
captures the current host policy. These settings never choose a UI workflow.

hooks.description: Hooks and Signing are "inherit" or "disabled"; signing also accepts "enabled".

GitSettingsPatch.description:
GitSettings is the git group of the shared settings document. Each operation
captures the current host policy. These settings never choose a UI workflow.

hooks.description: Hooks and Signing are "inherit" or "disabled"; signing also accepts "enabled".

HarnessEvent.description: Event is the envelope for everything a session emits.

data.description:
Data holds the typed payload for Type (see the *Data types). After
decoding from JSON, known types decode to their payload struct and
unknown types to json.RawMessage.

InputPart.description: InputPart is a text part or a local image reference in a prompt.

ListSessionsOptions.description:
ListOptions selects stored conversations. Empty filters preserve List's
original all-session behavior. Tags must all match; title matching is a
case-insensitive substring. SearchTranscript also searches event payloads.

LogGap.description: Gap describes dropped live records. There is no retained history to replay.

LogNotification.description: Notification carries exactly one record or dropped-record marker.

LogRecord.description:
Record is one normalized slog record. Attrs preserve nested groups and JSON
value types; keys such as "message" in attrs cannot replace envelope fields.

McpApproval.description: Approval says whether a server's tools need the host's approval.

McpConfig.description: Config is a set of MCP servers.

inheritNative.description:
InheritNative controls whether servers configured in the runtime
itself also load. Nil means yes.

McpEntry.description: Entry is one server in an Overview.

loaded.description: Loaded is false for servers that will not load (untrusted project file).

cwd.description:
Cwd is where to look for a project harness-kit.json (default: the
server's working directory).

runtimes.description:
Runtimes also lists the servers configured natively in these runtimes,
where supported (Codex).

enabled.description:
Enabled reports whether this server merges kit config files into
sessions (serve --kit-mcp). When false, Servers is empty.

McpServer.description:
Server is one MCP server: a local process (stdio) or a remote endpoint
(streamable HTTP).

disabled.description: Disabled removes the server, including one defined in a lower layer.

runtimes.description: Runtimes limits the server to these runtimes; empty means all.

source.description: Source is set by Resolve: "user", "project" or "session".

tools.description: Tools filters the server's tools by exact name.

pinned.description: Pinned is session-scoped: automatic eviction and suspension skip it.
Pinned is session-scoped: automatic eviction and suspension skip it.

MessageCompletedData.description: MessageCompletedData is a complete agent message.

MessageDeltaData.description: MessageDeltaData is an incremental chunk of an agent message.

parentCallId.description:
ParentCallID links messages from subagents to the tool call that
spawned them.

NativeMcp.description: NativeMCP lists one runtime's own MCP servers.

Outcome.description: Outcome is the host's answer to a request.

RawData.description: RawData wraps an unmapped native runtime message.

ReasoningCompletedData.description: ReasoningCompletedData is a complete reasoning block.

ReasoningDeltaData.description: ReasoningDeltaData is an incremental chunk of reasoning text or summary.

ResourceStats.description:
ResourceStats reports retained encoded event payloads, not process RSS.
Busy/pinned sessions and failed durable writes may defer resource reclamation.

runtimes.description: Runtimes limits discovery to these names; empty means all.

RuntimeSession.description: RuntimeSession is a session stored by a runtime.

RuntimeStatusData.description:
RuntimeStatusData reports runtime-level conditions (retries, rate limits,
warnings) that do not end the turn.

ServerCapabilities.description: ServerCapabilities describe what the server offers.

allowUnsafe.description:
AllowUnsafe reports whether the sidecar accepts session options that
disable runtime sandboxes or approvals.

eventLogSize.description: EventLogSize is the per-session replay window.

logs.description: Logs advertises opt-in structured slog notifications.

settings.description: Settings advertises the unified live settings API.

tools.description: Tools reports whether clients can register host tools.

SessionClosedData.description: SessionClosedData is the payload of session.closed.

cwd.description: Cwd is the working directory the agent operates in.

disableHostTools.description:
DisableHostTools gives the session no host tools, and no Harness Kit
MCP bridge at all (which also disables Claude Code approvals).

effort.description: Effort selects reasoning effort in the runtime's own vocabulary.

hostTools.description:
HostTools selects which of the host's registered tools (see package
tools) this session may use; nil means all of them.

instructions.description:
Instructions are appended to the runtime's own system/developer
instructions where supported.

mcp.description:
MCP lists MCP servers to add for this session, in Harness Kit's
portable format. ${VAR} references stay unexpanded here; adapters
resolve them when they start the runtime, so secrets are never
stored. Requires Capabilities.MCP.

model.description:
Model selects a model, in the runtime's own naming. Empty uses the
runtime's configured default.

options.description:
Options holds runtime-specific options: either the adapter's own
options struct, or JSON (json.RawMessage, []byte, map) that decodes
into it. See DecodeOptions.

rawEvents.description:
RawEvents asks the adapter to emit runtime.raw events for native
messages it does not map.

resumeId.description:
ResumeID is a runtime-native session ID to resume (a Codex thread
ID, a Claude Code session ID).

SessionConfigureParams.description:
SessionConfigureParams update defaults for subsequent turns. Config is
required; an empty object is a no-op. Omitted fields are unchanged.

SessionContext.description:
ContextInfo is a cached context observation. Reading it never starts a
runtime or makes an inference request. CanCompact is live session availability.

SessionDiffParams.description: SessionDiffParams reads a saved, bounded before/after turn diff.

archived.description:
Archived hides a conversation only when a caller requests that filter.
It is independent of runtime lifecycle and never cancels work.

config.description: Config is the current selection inherited by subsequent turns.

lastStatus.description: LastStatus is the status of the most recent finished turn.

pinned.description: Pinned prevents automatic cache eviction and runtime suspension.

settingsRevision.description: SettingsRevision changes only when session selections or pinning change.

title.description:
Title is a one-line name: the start of the first prompt, unless it
was set at creation or with Manager.Rename.

turns.description: Turns counts the prompts sent in this session.

SessionPinParams.description: SessionPinParams protect an idle session from automatic resource eviction.

turnId.description:
TurnID is optional; clients should generate it (e.g. a UUID) so they
can correlate events that arrive before the response.

SessionPromptResult.description:
SessionPromptResult is the result of "session.prompt". The turn runs
asynchronously; follow it through "event" notifications.

SessionRenameParams.description:
SessionRenameParams are the params of "session.rename". The result is a
SessionResult.

cwd.description: Cwd is the working directory the agent operates in.

disableHostTools.description:
DisableHostTools gives the session no host tools, and no Harness Kit
MCP bridge at all (which also disables Claude Code approvals).

effort.description: Effort selects reasoning effort in the runtime's own vocabulary.

hostTools.description:
HostTools selects which of the host's registered tools (see package
tools) this session may use; nil means all of them.

instructions.description:
Instructions are appended to the runtime's own system/developer
instructions where supported.

MCP lists MCP servers to add for this session, in Harness Kit's
portable format. ${VAR} references stay unexpanded here; adapters
resolve them when they start the runtime, so secrets are never
stored. Requires Capabilities.MCP.

model.description:
Model selects a model, in the runtime's own naming. Empty uses the
runtime's configured default.

options.description:
Options holds runtime-specific options: either the adapter's own
options struct, or JSON (json.RawMessage, []byte, map) that decodes
into it. See DecodeOptions.

rawEvents.description:
RawEvents asks the adapter to emit runtime.raw events for native
messages it does not map.

resumeId.description:
ResumeID is a runtime-native session ID to resume (a Codex thread
ID, a Claude Code session ID).

cwd.description: Cwd is the working directory the agent operates in.

disableHostTools.description:
DisableHostTools gives the session no host tools, and no Harness Kit
MCP bridge at all (which also disables Claude Code approvals).

effort.description: Effort selects reasoning effort in the runtime's own vocabulary.

anyOf.description:
HostTools selects which of the host's registered tools (see package
tools) this session may use; nil means all of them.

Instructions are appended to the runtime's own system/developer
instructions where supported.

anyOf.description:
MCP lists MCP servers to add for this session, in Harness Kit's
portable format. ${VAR} references stay unexpanded here; adapters
resolve them when they start the runtime, so secrets are never
stored. Requires Capabilities.MCP.

model.description:
Model selects a model, in the runtime's own naming. Empty uses the
runtime's configured default.

options.description:
Options holds runtime-specific options: either the adapter's own
options struct, or JSON (json.RawMessage, []byte, map) that decodes
into it. See DecodeOptions.

rawEvents.description:
RawEvents asks the adapter to emit runtime.raw events for native
messages it does not map.

resumeId.description:
ResumeID is a runtime-native session ID to resume (a Codex thread
ID, a Claude Code session ID).

SessionStartedData.description: SessionStartedData is the payload of session.started.

SessionState.description:
State is a session's lifecycle state.

	starting -> idle <-> running
	idle|running -> closing -> closed
	starting|idle|running -> failed   (the runtime died)

SessionUpdatedData.description:
SessionUpdatedData is a snapshot of the mutable session fields. Optional
fields that are absent have been cleared, rather than left unchanged.
State uses the session lifecycle names (idle, running, closing, ...).

config.description: Config contains current session defaults, never a one-turn override.

settingsRevision.description: SettingsRevision changes only when session settings or pinning change.

SettingsField.description:
Field describes a field for settings interfaces. When describes the global
lifetime; scoped snapshots can refine it using adapter capabilities.

SettingsGetParams.description: SettingsGetParams select host settings or a session's settings.

SettingsPatch.description: Omitted fields remain unchanged. Null disables nullable limits; false and zero are explicit values.

resync.description:
Resync means a slow observer missed one or more notifications, possibly
for another target. Refresh displayed targets with settings.get.

SettingsValues.description:
Values is the single settings document. Process describes host wiring and
shutdown policy; Session supplies defaults for new sessions. Scoped snapshots replace
Session with the selected session's settings. Optional limits use nil for no
limit; a zero cache budget retains no cached events. These are data budgets,
not limits on process RSS or memory owned by child processes.

StreamGapData.description: StreamGapData is the payload of stream.gap.

ToolCallParams.description: ToolCallParams are the params of the "tool.call" request.

ToolCompletedData.description: ToolCompletedData is the payload of tool.completed.

ToolContent.description: Content is one piece of tool output.

ToolFilter.description: ToolFilter limits which tools of a server may be used.

allow.description: Allow, if non-empty, is the complete list of usable tools.

deny.description: Deny lists tools that may never be used.

ToolOutputData.description: ToolOutputData is incremental tool output (e.g. command stdout).

ToolResult.description: Result is a tool's output, in MCP's CallToolResult shape.

approval.description: Approval "ask" requests the host's approval before each call.

inputSchema.description:
InputSchema is a JSON Schema for the arguments object (default
{"type":"object"}). Arguments are validated before tool.call.

ToolStartedData.description: ToolStartedData is the payload of tool.started.

ToolStatus.description: ToolStatus is the final status of a tool call.

TurnCompletedData.description:
TurnCompletedData is the payload of turn.completed. Exactly one
turn.completed is emitted for every turn.started.

TurnConfig.description:
Settings is a complete selection for a turn. Empty Model/Effort delegate
selection to the runtime. Options use the adapter's native names. Values are
replaced as a whole: there is no implicit recursive merge of native options.

TurnStartedData.description: TurnStartedData is the payload of turn.started.

config.description: Config is the accepted effective turn selection after native resolution.

input.description:
Input preserves content order and local image references for replay.
Image bytes are not copied into the transcript.

text.description: Text is the concatenated text of the prompt input.

TurnStatus.description: TurnStatus is the final status of a turn.

UsageData.description: UsageData reports token usage and, where the runtime provides it, cost.

costUsd.description: CostUSD is the runtime's own estimate, not a bill.

mode.description:
Mode is "snapshot" (default) or "delta". Snapshots are cumulative within
Scope and repeated snapshots are not additional usage. Deltas are increments.

tokensKnown.description:
TokensKnown distinguishes a reported zero from unknown token accounting.
ContextWindow is never a token-usage measurement.

totalTokens.description:
TotalTokens is the normalized consumed-token total, including cache reads
and writes where they are separate. Cached/reasoning counts may be subsets
of input/output; consumers must not add those fields to TotalTokens.

WorkspaceBinding.description:
Binding is durable identity data. Owned means the backend created a dedicated
worktree for SessionID; it is not permission to delete dirty files.

WorkspaceDiff.description:
Diff compares content at turn boundaries. WorkingTree includes nonignored
untracked files; Index separately shows changes to staged content.

WorkspaceSettings.description:
Settings is the workspace group in the kit's single settings document.
Location fields apply to new sessions; capture policy applies to future turns.

WorkspaceSettingsPatch.description:
Settings is the workspace group in the kit's single settings document.
Location fields apply to new sessions; capture policy applies to future turns.

WorkspaceSnapshot.description:
Snapshot references durable content objects in the repository. Capture does
not change the user's index, HEAD or worktree contents.
